learning_objective: 🎯 Deconstruct the Cartesian coordinate system, strictly plot dependent and independent variables, and mathematically analyze linear graphs to extract data and predict trends.

core_concepts.concept_title: 📐 The Anatomy of the Cartesian Plane
core_concepts.math_rule: The plane is defined by two perpendicular number lines: the horizontal x-axis and the vertical y-axis, intersecting perfectly at the Origin (0,0). Every point is defined by an ordered pair (x, y).
worked_example: 📝 Step 1: Plot the coordinate point P(4, 5) on graph paper.
⚙️ Step 2: Start precisely at the Origin (0,0). Move 4 units to the right along the horizontal x-axis.
Step 3: From that position, move 5 units vertically upward parallel to the y-axis and mark point P.

core_concepts.math_rule: In data graphing, the independent variable (the cause, such as Time) is strictly assigned to the horizontal x-axis, while the dependent variable (the effect, such as Distance or Temperature) is plotted on the vertical y-axis.
worked_example: 📝 Step 1: Graph the growth of a plant measured over 5 weeks.
⚙️ Step 2: Assign 'Weeks' (independent) to the x-axis. Assign 'Height in cm' (dependent) to the y-axis.
Step 3: Plot the corresponding (week, height) data pairs and observe the visual trajectory.

core_concepts.math_rule: A linear graph forms a perfectly straight unbroken line, representing a direct and constant proportional relationship between the x and y variables.
worked_example: 📝 Step 1: Analyze a linear graph showing cost vs. quantity of apples, passing through (0,0) and (2, 50).
⚙️ Step 2: Use the graph to find the cost of 4 apples by locating x=4 and tracking vertically to the line, then horizontally to the y-axis.
Step 3: The y-axis reads 100. Because it is a linear graph, the unit rate is strictly constant at ₹25 per apple.

common_pitfalls: ⚠️ Reversing the x and y coordinates when plotting, placing (3, 7) by moving 7 units right and 3 units up, which radically alters the mathematical data.
⚠️ Failing to maintain a uniform scale on an axis (e.g., jumping from 0 to 10, then 10 to 15, then 15 to 30), which mathematically distorts the entire visual representation.

real_world_application.title: 🌍 Financial Forecasting & Analytics
real_world_application.scenario: A financial analyst is tracking the compounding interest of an investment fund over a 10-year period to advise a client on potential returns.
real_world_application.math_connection: By plotting Time on the x-axis and Capital on the y-axis, the analyst generates a precise graph. If the interest is simple, it forms a linear graph; if compound, it forms a curve. The visual mathematical model instantly allows the client to predict their wealth at year 15 without running complex algebraic equations.

quick_recap: 💡 The x-coordinate dictates horizontal movement first, strictly followed by the y-coordinate for vertical movement.
💡 Independent variables dictate the horizontal baseline, while dependent variables react vertically.
💡 A straight continuous line on a graph mathematically guarantees a constant rate of change between the two measured quantities.
